extracted.intended_audience: foundation officers and trustees; philanthropy researchers; Hispanic nonprofit leaders and grantseekers
extracted.subtask_description: A research-focused rubric for measuring and improving how U.S. private foundations respond to Hispanic needs and Hispanic-run organizations, including empirical metrics of giving, institutional policies/procedures, and recommended research methods. Also includes a survey instrument for assessing foundation practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percent of total foundation dollars benefiting Hispanics
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure of the share of total foundation grant dollars that directly benefit Hispanics (reported in study: 1% for 1977-78).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Foundation Grants Index (FGI) data but note limitations and likely overstatement because FGI includes larger/more responsive foundations; mention comparability to prior studies (trend analysis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Concentration of giving among foundations (donor concentration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent to which a small number of foundations account for a large share of Hispanic-directed dollars (e.g., Ford Foundation provided 54% of support in study).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report share of total Hispanic funding by top N foundations; highlight risk of dependency on single major donor and compare top-donor amounts to next-ranked foundations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportion of foundations that make any grants to Hispanics
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentage (or count) of foundations in a population that awarded at least one grant for domestic Hispanic needs and concerns (study: less than one-fourth of foundations studied).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present both absolute number and percent; disaggregate by foundation size/type to show patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intensity of support per responsive foundation
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribution of number of grants per foundation to Hispanics (e.g., two-thirds gave only 1–2 grants; one-third gave 3+ grants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use frequency counts of grants per foundation and classify foundations by intensity categories (1–2, 3+).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trend in number and intensity of foundations giving to Hispanics
rubrics_metrics.description: Change over time in count of foundations supporting Hispanics and in the number/size of grants they provide (compare to prior studies like 1972–74).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contextualize increases/decreases, but note whether added foundations gave only 1–2 small grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Share of funds going to Hispanic-controlled recipient agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Percent (and dollar amount) of Hispanic-designated grant monies that are awarded to agencies controlled by Hispanics (study: 51% of money to Hispanic-run organizations; 59% of grants to Hispanic-controlled agencies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare to past figures; note whether grants are sole-to-Hispanic agencies vs mixed recipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whether foundations contribute solely to Hispanic, solely to non-Hispanic, or to both types of recipient agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Categorize foundations by whether their Hispanic-related giving goes only to Hispanic-controlled agencies, only to non-Hispanic agencies, or to both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this to profile foundations' patterns and to identify those that focus exclusively on Hispanic organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic distribution of Hispanic grants relative to Hispanic population
rubrics_metrics.description: Regional allocation of Hispanic-directed grant dollars compared to the regional distribution of the Hispanic population (e.g., Northeast received disproportionate share relative to its Hispanic population).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map dollars and percent shares by region; identify regions underserved relative to population (e.g., Texas, New Mexico, North Central), and note regions receiving none.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fields of interest prioritized in Hispanic grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Breakdown of grant dollars across fields (education, legal advocacy, research, community development, health services, social services, cultural activities, religion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report dollar amounts, percent of total Hispanic dollars, and rank; identify whether funds concentrate in traditional/low-risk fields (education) vs other areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethnicity categorization of beneficiaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify grants by beneficiary ethnicity: Chicano (Mexican-American), Puerto Rican, General Hispanic, Mixed (Hispanic and other minorities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use consistent definitions; document assumptions used for classification and be transparent about ambiguous cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concentration of funds among Hispanic donees
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent to which a small number of Hispanic organizations receive a large share of Hispanic-directed funds (e.g., MALDEF obtained almost one-third of monies to Hispanic-controlled agencies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List top recipient organizations with counts and dollar amounts; consider implications for equity and capacity-building.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foundation size/assets as predictor of responsiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Correlation between foundation asset size and likelihood/amount of support for Hispanics (study: foundations with assets >$1M more likely to support Hispanics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disaggregate response rates and giving by asset-size bins; avoid assuming causation without further analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foundation type profile (community, corporate, family, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess over- or under-representation of foundation types among those responsive to Hispanics (e.g., community foundations over-represented; corporate foundations under-represented).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare distribution of types in sample to universe of foundations to identify atypical patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence of full-time administrative staff
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a foundation has full-time staff (indicator: responsive foundations reported 92% with full-time staff).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use staff presence/size as a proxy for capacity to engage, solicit, and administer grants; report approximate staff counts where available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hispanic full-time employees
rubrics_metrics.description: Number or presence of full-time staff of Hispanic origin in the foundation (study: 12% of responsive foundations reported full-time Hispanic employees).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report counts and roles; use as an indicator of cultural competence and outreach capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Hispanic consultants
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the foundation uses Hispanic consultants (study: 17% reported using Hispanic consultants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track consultant usage and role (advisory, outreach, evaluation) as part of institutional practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hispanic representation on boards of trustees
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence and number of persons of Hispanic origin serving as board members (study: 12% of responsive foundations had Hispanic trustees; Council on Foundations estimate for all foundations was 0.3%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report counts by Hispanic subgroup where available; consider board composition as a governance indicator for responsiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and transparency practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether foundation issues annual, biennial, or other reports and the degree of information provided (responsive foundations: 83% published annual/biennial reports vs 2% in general).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate quality of reporting: inclusion of grant purposes, donee names/contacts, dollar amounts, and program descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mailing list practices and targeted outreach
rubrics_metrics.description: Existence of general mailing lists, special Hispanic mailing lists, and inclusion-on-request policies (study: 72% claimed mailing lists open to Hispanics; only 11% had special Hispanic lists).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether lists are accessible to prospective applicants and whether foundations proactively maintain targeted outreach lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsiveness to applicant inquiries and provision of application information
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether foundations respond to letters of inquiry and whether they provide details such as application deadlines, specific suggestions on proposal contents/length/format, and dates when Executive Board meets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record rates of responsiveness; note that responsiveness declines for more complex inquiries (dates, formats).

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement and rejection communication practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether foundations send written acknowledgements of proposals received and whether they send written rejection notices (study: 88% acknowledged proposals; 95% sent written rejections).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate timeliness and clarity of communications; encourage written feedback when rejecting proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation of reasons for proposal rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether foundations explain to unsuccessful applicants why a proposal was not funded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track whether foundations provide substantive reasons and whether they offer suggestions for improvement or alternate funding routes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of feedback on preliminary drafts or concept papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether foundations provide feedback on early-stage materials (study: 64% reported offering feedback).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider feedback as an indicator of willingness to develop grantee capacity; note limitations if feedback is selective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advice on other funding sources and technical assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether foundations advise applicants about alternate funders and whether they provide staff or services expressly to strengthen applicants' fundraising/management capacity (study: 44% offered advice on other sources; 25% had staff to provide technical assistance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate between routine referral advice and dedicated capacity-building support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical foundation actions for promising but poorly drafted proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Set of possible institutional responses when an applicant proposes a worthy idea but the written proposal is weak (options in survey: reject; encourage revision; no further advice; request additional information; offer technical assistance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use frequency of each action to assess flexibility and grantee development orientation; encourage proactive assistance where feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended advice for minority applicant self-improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Advice foundations suggested minority applicants could use: study and adhere to foundation guidelines (21%), conduct research to target foundations better (14%), improve proposal contents and structure (17%), and strengthen management/budgeting/fundraising capabilities (14%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these as checklist items for training programs and for applicants preparing submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for educational research and development activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether and which types of educational R&D activities foundations support (internships, graduate/postdoctoral fellowships, conferences, surveys, community needs assessments, ongoing research by organizations/individuals, publication, seminars/workshops).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track both current support and historical support over past five years; disaggregate by activity type and by whether recipients were Hispanics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey instrument items as institutional indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of specific survey questions to profile foundations: type of foundation, asset-size categories, total grants in year, average grant size, staffing, publications, mailing lists, responsiveness, technical assistance, educational R&D support, Hispanic board/staff/consultants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The questionnaire (Appendix H) supplies a standardized set of items for cross-foundation comparison and can be adapted for contemporary surveys.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Foundation Grants Index (FGI) with verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation to use the FGI to identify grants but to verify entries via telephone/mail contact and annual reports because FGI contains inaccuracies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do manual checks, spot checks, telephone calls to donees/foundations, and correct FGI errors when found; do not rely exclusively on IRS 990 data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improving Foundation Center/Fri data quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions should examine and improve the Foundation Center's coding and description systems; foundations should assist by checking bi-monthly listings and reporting errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocate collaboration among NCRP, Council on Foundations, and Foundation Center to improve coding consistency and data accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research resource and credibility standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific research on foundation grantmaking requires substantial time and funds, access to reliable public records, cooperation from foundations, and use of multiple data sources to ensure credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers should plan for resources to do telephone/mail follow-ups, gather annual reports, and cross-check data; NCRP should advise on measures to ensure study credibility; Council on Foundations should help raise response rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency recommendation for foundations' annual reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Foundations should include informative descriptions of grant purposes and names/addresses/telephone numbers of donees in their Annual Reports to improve public record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend standard fields to include so researchers and applicants can better identify relevant grants and contacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification assumptions for coding Hispanic grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Operational assumptions used when classifying grants as Hispanic-related: agencies with 'La Raza' considered Chicano; legal names referencing Puerto Rican culture considered Puerto Rican; institutions so assumed are treated as minority-controlled; bilingual/bicultural services in high-Hispanic areas assumed related to Hispanics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document and test these assumptions via telephone confirmation of donees; be explicit about assumptions in reporting and subject them to spot-check validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regional grouping definitions for analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Grouping of states into regions for geographic analysis (Northeast, North Central, Southwest, National) with explicit state lists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use consistent regional definitions; indicate limitations where grant location cannot be clearly determined from FGI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Card-based manual data extraction and cross-checking protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Manual method used in study: one card per grant; color-coded card sets organized by grantee, by foundation, by ethnicity, and by field; multi-pass checking for omissions, duplicates, and errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use independent enumerators for cross-checks, photocopy card sets in different colors for parallel analyses, and perform spot checks against source data and telephone verification.
